summary: Phase 5c-i-δ — wired the wallet to the Nostr network on opt-in. Added nostrTransportEnabled pref (default false), a Mycelium-network Settings toggle with a privacy explainer, a WalletProvider transport lifecycle (dynamic import so non-opting users pay zero bytes), and an InboxPanel surface at the top of the People tab. All eight gates green; pushed branch only.

why.text: Phase 5c-i-α/-β/-γ shipped the cryptography, the wire client, and the Wallet-internal seam — but the wallet still never talked to a relay. This cut closes that loop on opt-in. Default-off because subscribing exposes the wallet pubkey to public relays (real metadata leak); the toggle gives the operator the choice with the trade-off named. Dynamic import keeps the WebSocket+NIP-44 stack out of the bundle for users who never opt in.

files_changed: scripts/bundle-budget.mjs (named the transport chunk + parseEnvelope helper)
outcome.notes: Pushed to claude/compare-library-wallet-OW5FF as commit 2679e13. NOT pushed to main. WalletProvider chunk landed at 5.33 KB gz of 5.5 KB budget — tight; further additions will probably need code-splitting too. transport opt-in chunk 1.6 KB gz of 5 KB budget. Pre-existing tapit-attest tamper-byte flake (1/256) still relevant. NIP-44 interop verification still outstanding — most urgent now because the next operator field test will actually hit real relays.

uncertainty: Real-relay round-trip behavior has not been exercised yet. The WebSocket reconnect logic is unit-tested via injected fakes but not against a live relay. Two-device test with two real wallets opting in would close the loop; that is the natural smoke test the operator can run when ready. NIP-44 byte-for-byte interop with third-party Nostr clients is still untested against the upstream reference vectors.
ripple: wallet-core — WalletProvider now manages a third lifecycle (anchorWorker, transport)
connections — once routing arrives (next cut), incoming handshakes/memberships can complete remotely without the operator pasting JSON
settings — added a toggle the operator can now flip; the wallet visibly becomes network-active or not based on it
next: Cut Phase 5c-i-ε — auto-route incoming envelopes to the matching modal (cosign as witness for unsigned handshakes, absorb-cosign for counter-signed handshakes, membership receive for credential-kind envelopes). Also: run the NIP-44 reference vectors before any real-relay field test.
